items.title: GNPC Explorco showcases Voltaian Basin exploration potential at AOW:Energy 2026
items.description: Ghana’s national exploration company, GNPC Explorco, has showcased the investment and exploration potential of the Voltaian Basin as the country seeks to attract fresh investment into its upstream petroleum sector. The presentation was made during Ghana Day at AOW:Energy 2026 in Accra, which brought together governments, national oil companies, international operators, investors and financial institutions from across Africa’s energy sector. Speaking during the session, Managing Director of GNPC Explorco, Sam Opoku Arthur, highlighted the strategic importance of the Voltaian Basin to Ghana’s exploration agenda. He outlined the basin’s geological potential and the opportunities it presents for investors and strategic partners. The Voltaian Basin is Ghana’s principal onshore frontier basin and remains one of the country’s least explored petroleum provinces. GNPC Explorco said it is advancing work in the basin to improve geological understanding, reduce exploration risk and create opportunities for credible partners to participate in the next phase of Ghana’s upstream development. Mr Opoku Arthur stressed the importance of technical expertise, collaboration and strategic investment in unlocking the potential of frontier basins. “The Voltaian Basin represents an exciting frontier for Ghana’s exploration future. Our focus is to systematically unlock its potential through technical excellence, responsible exploration and strategic partnerships,” he said. “We believe there is a compelling opportunity for credible investors and partners to join us in writing this next chapter of Ghana’s upstream story.” The Ghana Day programme also featured keynote addresses from the Minister for Energy and Green Transition, the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) and the Chief Executive Officer of the Petroleum Commission. Their presentations provided perspectives on Ghana’s upstream investment environment and the country’s broader energy ambitions. For Ghana, development of the Voltaian Basin could help diversify the country’s exploration portfolio beyond its existing offshore producing fields. GNPC Explorco said its participation at AOW:Energy 2026 forms part of efforts to engage the international investment community and build partnerships capable of advancing frontier exploration. The company is particularly seeking credible technical and financial partners to support exploration and potential development in Ghana’s underexplored basins. It said such activities would be pursued with an emphasis on responsible exploration and delivering sustainable value to the country.

items.title: Cherté du carburant en France : les pêcheurs bloquent des ports, quel impact sur l’Algérie ?
items.description: La hausse des prix de l'énergie est en train de tourner à la crise sociale en France. Dans une action d’envergure et concertée, plusieurs ports sur la côte méditerranéenne dont celui de Sète ont été bloqués ce mardi 15 septembre par des pêcheurs excédés par les charges qui étouffent leur activité et la dégradation de leurs conditions de travail. Les compagnies maritimes (GNV, Algérie Ferries et Corsica Linea) qui desservent l’Algérie à partir du port de Sète n’ont pas fait état de blocage de leurs traversées ou de désagréments. La hausse des prix du carburant, dans un contexte mondial marqué par des tensions sur l'énergie et la flambée des cours de pétrole, affecte sensiblement les automobilistes et des pans entiers de l’économie française. Un terminal pétrolier bloqué à Fos-sur-Mer Le mouvement a été lancé lundi par les comités régionaux de pêche d'Occitanie, de la région Paca et de Corse et des syndicats de marins. Ses initiateurs ont indiqué que ce mouvement commun « se poursuivra tant que des réponses concrètes n'auront pas été apportées aux principales revendications de la profession ». L’action la plus notable a eu lieu dans les Bouches-du-Rhône où le terminal pétrolier de Fos-sur-Mer a été bloqué ce mardi à 3h du matin par une cinquantaine de pêcheurs, empêchant des dizaines de camions citernes d'accéder dans l’enceinte. La levée du blocage a eu lieu vers 10h, après l’intervention des CRS, selon l’AFP. “L’Europe nous tue” A Sète, port important de transport de voyageurs sur la Méditerranée, une action similaire a eu lieu ce mardi. Les protestataires ont bloqué les ferries amarrés sur le quai. Les navires qui arrivent sont autorisés à débarquer leurs passagers mais pas à quitter l’enceinte. Les autres ports bloqués sont ceux de Port-La Nouvelle (Aude) et Port-Vendres (Pyrénées-Orientales), où a eu lieu la première action de blocage dès lundi. « L'Europe nous tue », « L’UE coule nos bateaux et Paris nous regarde », ont scandé les pêcheurs qui ont bloqué le terminal de Fos-sur-Mer. Le ministère de la Mer et de la Pêche a indiqué à l’AFP que la ministre Catherine Chabaud a pris acte des revendications des pêcheurs et les recevra dans les prochains jours. Sur BFMTV, le président du comité stratégique des supermarchés E.Leclerc a exclu un risque de pénurie à ce stade mais a concédé que “cela ne fera que paralyser”, jugeant que le blocage d'un port pétrolier “n’est pas logique”. Quel impact sur les traversées de et vers l’Algérie ? On ne sait pas à ce stade si la situation affecte ou non les liaisons avec les ports algériens. Aucune des compagnies qui desservent l’Algérie n’a fait état de perturbations de son programme en lien avec le mouvement de protestation. Lundi, Algérie Ferries a annoncé le report à mercredi de la traversée Marseille – Oran prévue ce mardi à bord du ferry El Djazaïr II, indiquant que la décision est due à des raisons indépendantes de sa volonté, sans plus de détails. Le port de Marseille n’est pas cité dans les comptes-rendus des médias français parmi les enceintes bloquées. items.title: Dafeamekpor calls for forensic audit after alleged GH¢600m COVID-19 fumigation gap
items.description: Majority Chief Whip in Parliament, Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor, is calling for a forensic audit of Ghana’s COVID-19 expenditure following evidence suggesting that more than GH¢600 million in fumigation spending may have been left out of the Auditor-General’s special audit. He said the alleged gap raises fresh questions about the completeness of the COVID-19 expenditure review and requires the government to reopen the matter. “If an independent inquiry had been done by a media person, and it’s been established that as much as 600 million or more in expenditure had not been audited, then what it means is that we may have to now call for a forensic audit,” he said on Joy FM’s Top Story on Tuesday, September 15. According to Mr Dafeamekpor, the COVID-19 audit was already considered inadequate by members of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), who had raised concerns that it was hurriedly conducted. “If you recall, like David said, when these matters came up for our scrutiny, we discovered that one, the audit was hurriedly done, and two, because it was hurriedly done, some expenditure lines were not even covered under the audit,” he said. He added,“at the time, when we called for a more comprehensive audit of the COVID-19 accounts, we were told that we were opposition and we were asking for an audit when the audit had already been done.” Mr Dafeamekpor said a forensic audit would go beyond the work covered by the special audit and examine both expenditure lines that were inadequately reviewed and those that were not audited at all. He said such an exercise was necessary to bring closure to continuing questions over the use of public funds during the COVID-19 emergency. “We can bring closure to this matter, because the COVID-19 expenditure issues keep coming up, and it’s as if we haven’t done a good job in examining how and holding accountable public officers who, under emergency powers, under emergency circumstances, were given so much public money to expend, and now accountability has become an issue,” he said. Mr Dafeamekpor, who previously served on the PAC, said he would support a forensic audit to settle the outstanding questions. “So where I sit, I will have to ask for a forensic audit to be done, and it will be good that that is done so that everybody’s mind will be put to rest on the matter,” he said.

items.title: 2027: Ex-Nasarawa Speaker begs defectors to return to APC
items.description: The immediate past Speaker, Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Alhaji Ibrahim Balarabe, has appealed to all aggrieved members who defected from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to other parties to return to the party. He said the appeal became imperative in view of the fact that they laboured to build a house, only to vacate it “at the time you need it most.” The former speaker made the call in an interview with newsmen in Lafia on Tuesday. Balarabe’s call followed the recent defection of the immediate past Chairman of Toto Local Government Area, Aliyu Abdullahi, from the APC. The News Agency of Nigeria recalls that on September 14, the former chairman announced his resignation from the ruling APC. The former speaker advocated for calm among APC members in Toto local government area. Balarabe, who disagreed with the move by the former chairman, enjoined him to set aside whatever grievances and opt for dialogue, to resolve their differences amicably. He also urged him to withdraw the resignation letter earlier issued and return to the APC. “You cannot leave the house you have built for another person to inherit. “APC is our home, it is our party, and our victory is assured by the will of Allah. We will get there. We will deliver our LGA In-Sha-Allah, come 2027. “We cannot fold our hands and watch our party lose its members. We cannot fold our hands and allow our people to leave. “In politics, everyone matters. The grassroots matter because politics is local, this is a fact,” Balarabe said. The former speaker observed that success of APC as a party in the area come 2027, solidly depends on the unity and peace among the party members in the area. “Unity of purpose is paramount for the task ahead of us, and no matter what, we must unite our people to facilitate victory in 2027,” he added. items.title: Minority demands itemised accounts for GHS50m South Africa evacuation, pulls out of closed-door meeting
items.description: The Minority Caucus on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee has pulled out of a closed-door meeting scheduled for Wednesday, September 16, over the Foreign Ministry’s failure to provide detailed expenditure records for the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa. The Caucus says the Ministry has yet to furnish it with the itemised account and supporting documents it requested under the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989). The Foreign Affairs Minister, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, is expected to brief the Committee on the evacuation exercise at the meeting. In a statement issued on Tuesday, September 15, and signed by the Ranking Member of the Committee, Samuel A. Jinapor, the Minority said it would not participate in the meeting unless the requested records are provided. According to the statement, the Minority submitted a formal RTI request to the Ministry on August 17, 2026, under reference number MP/BF/RTI/2026/007. The request was received by the Ministry on August 25. The Caucus said it sought comprehensive information and supporting records on the cost and financing of the evacuation exercise. Among the documents requested were details of expenditure incurred, sources of funding, the identities and contributions of private partners, spending on flights and other transportation, accommodation, feeding, medical services and reintegration payments. The Minority also requested relevant procurement and payment records. On September 7, the Foreign Affairs Minister announced that almost GH¢50 million had been spent on the evacuation and reintegration of 1,964 Ghanaians. The Minority, however, says it has not received the supporting records behind the figure. “To date, however, the Ministry has not furnished the Minority with the itemised account and supporting documentation requested,” the statement said. The Minority stressed that it supported the government’s decision to evacuate Ghanaians whose safety and welfare were threatened by xenophobic attacks in South Africa. “The protection of Ghanaian citizens abroad is an important responsibility of the State, and our support for measures taken to secure their safety has never been in doubt,” it said. It nevertheless argued that support for the evacuation does not remove the government’s obligation to account for public funds spent on the exercise. That support, it said, “cannot dispense with the equally important obligation of Government to account fully and transparently for the expenditure of public funds.” The Caucus said it was therefore not appropriate to participate in a closed-door briefing on the evacuation while its formal request for the underlying expenditure records remained outstanding. “The Minority Caucus on the Foreign Affairs Committee of Parliament will not participate in the closed-door meeting scheduled for Wednesday, 16th September 2026, unless and until the Ministry provides the itemised account and supporting records requested,” it said. The Minority has reiterated its call on the Foreign Ministry to disclose the full expenditure relating to the evacuation exercise. It said it would continue to exercise its constitutional and parliamentary responsibility to demand transparency and accountability in the use of taxpayers’ funds. “That responsibility is owed not only to Parliament, but ultimately to the Ghanaian people whose resources are being expended,” the statement said.

items.title: Effiduase Asokore MP sues Rev. Owusu Bempah for GH¢10m over alleged defamatory comments
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Effiduase-Asokore, Dr. Nana Ayew Afriye, has sued Rev. Isaac Owusu Bempah, Head Pastor of Glorious Word Power Ministry International, and his church for GH¢10 million over alleged defamatory remarks. The suit, filed at the Accra High Court, relates to statements allegedly made by the pastor during a church service on September 6, 2026, which were later circulated on social media. In his statement of claim, Dr. Ayew Afriye, a medical doctor and third-term MP on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party who chaired Parliament’s Health Committee from 2021 to January 2025 and now serves as its Ranking Member, said Rev. Owusu Bempah accused him and other NPP figures of plotting to attack him and his church. The writ quotes the pastor as alleging that some individuals, including Dr. Ayew Afriyie, planned to convey two buses of people from the Ashanti Region to Accra to attack his church. Dr. Ayew Afriye denies the claim, stating he has never conspired with anyone or attempted to organize any attack against Rev. Owusu Bempah or his church. He contends the statement is defamatory and intended to injure his reputation as a medical practitioner, legislator and public figure. He further believes the viral statement has caused him embarrassment, public ridicule and potential damage to his political standing in Effiduase-Asokore. According to the writ, a video of the alleged statements was published on social media, expanding its reach. The MP said he publicly called on Rev. Owusu Bempah to retract and apologize if he could not substantiate the allegations, but the pastor instead indicated in a media interview that he was ready to meet him in court. Dr. Ayew Afriye is therefore asking the court to declare the statements defamatory, award GH¢10 million in damages, order a retraction and unqualified apology on the same platforms where the statements were published, and grant a perpetual injunction restraining the defendants from making similar statements against him. He is also seeking costs, including legal fees.

items.title: Air Algérie signe un accord avec les pilotes de ligne : voici les objectifs
items.description: En plus du renforcement de sa flotte, de l’élargissement de son réseau et la modernisation de ses services, Air Algérie vise aussi à améliorer les conditions de travail de ses salariés. Pour ce faire, la compagnie a signé un accord avec le Syndicat des pilotes de ligne algériens (SPLA). C’est ce que dévoile un communiqué commun publié ce mardi 15 septembre. Il a été signé conjointement par la direction générale d’ Air Algérie et le Syndicat des pilotes de ligne algériens (SPLA). Cette démarche est présentée comme un pas de plus “dans le processus de réforme et de développement amorcé par le groupe”. Pilotes : que prévoit l’accord entre Air Algérie et le SPLA ? Avec cet accord, Air Algérie veut “renforcer ses capacités opérationnelles et améliorer la qualité de ses services conformément au plus haut niveau des normes dans le secteur du transport aérien”. Concrètement, cet accord “vise à améliorer les conditions professionnelles et sociales des pilotes d’Air Algérie et de leur garantir un environnement de travail plus adapté à l’exercice de leurs missions, ce qui va contribuer à améliorer la performance et à enraciner la culture de la compétence et du professionnalisme” au sein de la compagnie aérienne nationale. Le communiqué évoque une volonté d’Air Algérie et du syndicat des pilotes de ligne de s’en tenir à “un dialogue social responsable et constructif fondé sur la confiance et le respect mutuel”, et ce, afin de pouvoir “mobiliser l’ensemble des compétences et de renforcer les relations professionnelles et sociales”. Qu’en pense le syndicat ? De son côté, le syndicat réaffirme sa conviction que la modernisation de la compagnie ne peut se faire sans “l’investissement dans les ressources humaines, l’instauration d’un dialogue social sérieux et responsable, basé sur la confiance et le respect mutuel et une collaboration constructive”. Aux yeux du SPLA, cet accord est “une étape importante qui mène vers l’amélioration des conditions professionnelles et sociales des pilotes”. Cette démarche va aussi leur permettre, toujours selon le syndicat, “d’accomplir leurs missions dans les meilleures conditions”. Mais si le communiqué évoque “une amélioration des conditions professionnelles et sociales” des pilotes, il reste discret sur les décisions concrètes comme la revalorisation des salaires, la révision des heures de vol ou de nouveaux acquis sociaux. Cet accord avec les pilotes n’est toutefois que le début d’une “démarche globale d’un dialogue social” qu’Air Algérie veut mener avec ses “différents corps et catégories professionnelles”, et ce, afin de parvenir à “un équilibre entre les exigences du développement et de la stabilité de l’entreprise et l’amélioration des conditions professionnelles”, lit-on sur le communiqué. items.title: Hervé Renard : « Le Maroc est la sélection africaine la plus en vue au monde »
items.description: Les performances réalisées par les Lions de l’Atlas ces dernières années continuent de susciter les éloges sur la scène internationale. Pour Hervé Renard, le Maroc s’est aujourd’hui installé comme la principale référence du football africain et fait partie des sélections les plus suivies au niveau mondial. Invité de l’émission « Talents d’Afrique » , diffusée lundi sur Canal+ Sport, le sélectionneur français de la Côte d’Ivoire a placé le Maroc au sommet de la hiérarchie africaine. « Le Maroc est la sélection numéro un en Afrique dans les compétitions internationales, personne ne peut le nier », a affirmé Hervé Renard, en mettant notamment en avant la régularité des Lions de l’Atlas lors des grandes compétitions. Le technicien français a rappelé le parcours historique réalisé par la sélection marocaine lors du Mondial 2022, conclu par une qualification pour les demi-finales, ainsi que sa présence en quarts de finale de l’édition 2026. Pour Renard, ces résultats ont contribué à changer la perception du football africain à l’échelle internationale. « Nous devons croire aux capacités de ces équipes, car il y a une très grande qualité dans le football africain », a-t-il souligné. Renard salue l’organisation du Maroc L’ancien sélectionneur des Lions de l’Atlas, qui a dirigé la sélection marocaine pendant trois ans et demi, estime également que les progrès du football national reposent sur une organisation solide. « Le Maroc dispose d'un système et d'une organisation de très haut niveau et il n'a rien à envier aux meilleures équipes du monde » , a-t-il déclaré. Une évolution qui, selon lui, s’inscrit dans une dynamique durable. « Le Maroc a bien compris les choses et s’inscrit dans une dynamique ascendante », a ajouté le technicien français. À ses yeux, l’exemple marocain pourrait servir de modèle aux autres sélections du continent. Mais pour reproduire cette progression, des investissements importants restent nécessaires, notamment dans les infrastructures et les moyens consacrés au développement du football. Hervé Renard considère ainsi que la réussite du Maroc doit encourager les autres nations africaines à croire davantage en leur potentiel. Le football du continent dispose, selon lui, d’une génération de jeunes joueurs capables de rivaliser avec les meilleures équipes mondiales. « Il y a toute une génération de jeunes africains qui rêvent de parvenir au sommet du football mondial et ils ont les moyens d'y arriver, mais ils doivent croire en leurs capacités » , a-t-il conclu. Une reconnaissance particulière pour le football marocain de la part d’un technicien qui connaît parfaitement son fonctionnement, après avoir occupé le poste de sélectionneur des Lions de l’Atlas et conduit la Côte d’Ivoire depuis le banc. The post Hervé Renard : « Le Maroc est la sélection africaine la plus en vue au monde » appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Sécurité routière : Le non-port du casque sera sanctionné dès le 1er octobre
items.description: À l’approche de la rentrée scolaire, le ministère de la Sécurité annonce la fin de la période de tolérance concernant le port du casque de protection. À compter du 1er octobre 2026, tout conducteur d’un engin motorisé à deux ou trois roues circulant sans casque s’exposera aux sanctions prévues par la réglementation en vigueur. Dans un communiqué publié ce 15 septembre 2026, le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana, rappelle l’importance du respect des règles de sécurité routière, particulièrement en cette période de rentrée scolaire, marquée par une intensification du trafic et une hausse des risques d’accidents. Le ministre salue, par ailleurs, la prise de conscience d’une large majorité des usagers concernant le port du casque. Il précise toutefois que la période de tolérance administrative prendra fin le 30 septembre prochain. Durant cette période, les contrevenants étaient principalement sensibilisés et refoulés, sans faire l’objet de sanctions. Dès le 1er octobre, le non-port du casque sera donc sanctionné par une amende de 3 000 francs CFA, assortie de l’immobilisation de l’engin jusqu’à la présentation d’un casque de protection. Les services compétents ont été instruits de procéder à des contrôles rigoureux afin d’assurer la stricte application de cette mesure. À travers cette décision, le ministère de la Sécurité entend contribuer à la préservation des vies humaines, notamment celles des élèves et étudiants, et faire de la sécurité routière une responsabilité partagée entre tous les usagers de la route. items.title: Matoto : un bébé d’une semaine porté disparu dans un dispensaire, une femme enceinte suspectée
items.description: Screenshot " data-large-file="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/IMG_8595.jpeg?fit=1024%2C592&ssl=1" /> Un cas de disparition présumée d’un nouveau-né a été signalé ce mardi 15 septembre 2026 au dispensaire-maternité Saint Gabriel, situé à Matoto Centre. Le nourrisson, une fille âgée d’à peine une semaine, s’était rendue dans cet établissement avec sa mère pour des soins au niveau du nombril. Selon les informations recueillies, une femme présentée comme étant enceinte est suspectée d’avoir emporté le bébé. La mère de l’enfant, Manamè Sanoh, serait originaire d’Antag, dans la commune de Tombolia. Selon Ibrahima Sory Sanoh, oncle de la mère du nourrisson, les deux femmes se sont rencontrés dans la cour du dispensaire après les soins du bébé avant de quitter les lieux. « Le nourrisson disparu souffrait d’une plaie au nombril. La suspecte et la mère de l’enfant auraient fait des soins ensemble au sein du dispensaire avant de sortir de la cour, l’une en compagnie de l’autre. À la devanture de l’hôpital, en partance pour la Plaque où elles devaient s’embarquer, la nourrice se serait retournée pour aller aux toilettes du dispensaire. À son retour sur le lieu où elle avait laissé l’inconnue, aucun signe de vie des deux. À l’entame des recherches, les riverains questionnés sur le sujet ont soutenu penser que la suspecte était familière à la nourrice, vu qu’elles avaient été aperçues ensemble. » Quelques heures après les faits, une plainte aurait été déposée auprès du service de l’Office de protection du genre, de l’enfant et des mœurs (OPROGEM) de proximité afin de permettre l’ouverture d’une enquête et de retrouver le nouveau-né. Les circonstances exactes de cette disparition restent à établir. Nous y reviendrons… Marie Mayi CISSÉ L’article Matoto : un bébé d’une semaine porté disparu dans un dispensaire, une femme enceinte suspectée est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Forestry Commission arrests 12 illegal miners, impounds three excavators in South Formangso Forest Reserve
items.description: The Forestry Commission has arrested 12 suspected illegal miners and impounded three excavators during an operation in the South Formangso Forest Reserve in the Ashanti Region. The operation, conducted on September 13, 2026, also resulted in the seizure of six water-pumping machines, while six Chanfang machines found at the site were destroyed. The arrested suspects were handed over to the Juaso Police for further investigation. Personnel from the Ashanti Regional Office and the Juaso District Office of the Forestry Commission reportedly detected the presence of the illegal miners in the reserve and mobilised the Commission’s Rapid Response Team. According to the Juaso District Forestry Manager, Isaac Boamah Amanquah, the miners were operating with heavy-duty equipment and posed a security risk to forestry personnel. “Early morning of 13th September 2026, my field officer, who is in charge of the South Formangso Forest Reserve, informed me about illegal miners entering the forest reserve to a community called Kagyebi Romanuso to do their normal illegal activities,” he said. Mr Amanquah said he quickly mobilised personnel to the area, where they found three excavators being used by the miners. The excavators were subsequently transported to the Forestry Commission’s Range Quarters at Asankare. “Their activities are a threat to our forestry staff. Because when they dig the holes, they don’t cover them, and it makes patrolling very difficult for us, and the area destroyed is estimated to be two hectares,” he said. The Forestry Commission says the latest operation is not the first time illegal miners have invaded the South Formangso Forest Reserve. The Juaso District of the Forestry Services Division reportedly conducted a similar operation last year, during which makeshift structures and equipment belonging to illegal miners were destroyed. However, the Commission said the miners later returned to the protected area by reshaping an old access road and using it to move Chanfang machines and excavators into the reserve. Mr Amanquah has warned persons planning to engage in illegal mining within the reserve to stay away, stressing that the Commission is maintaining a zero-tolerance approach to activities that degrade protected forest areas. “To me all those who have intentions to enter the reserve to carry out illegal mining operations, I want them to know that the Juaso Forest District, our eyes are on them 24/7. And anybody who will be caught will face the full rigorous law,” he said. The Forestry Commission has meanwhile intensified patrols and monitoring operations in the area to deter further incursions and protect the ecological integrity of the South Formangso Forest Reserve.

items.title: NAF takes delivery of five new helicopters
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has taken delivery of five new helicopters as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to modernise and re-equip the Armed Forces to confront evolving security threats. The newly acquired platforms comprise three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters manufactured by Leonardo Helicopters of Italy and two H-125 helicopters produced by Airbus Helicopters. A statement by the NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said the acquisition was part of the Federal Government’s sustained investment in strengthening the operational capabilities of the service. Ejodame said the three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters arrived in Lagos on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, as part of a batch of 10 recently acquired by the Federal Government. He said the remaining seven helicopters were expected to be delivered before the end of 2026. The two H-125 helicopters had earlier been delivered to the NAF, bringing the total number of helicopters covered by the latest acquisition to five. Reacting to the development, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, described the acquisition as another milestone in the Federal Government’s ongoing investment in the modernisation and re-equipment of the NAF. Aneke said the arrival of the helicopters would increase aircraft availability and give commanders greater flexibility in deploying airpower in support of ongoing military operations across the country. According to him, the new platforms would particularly strengthen the NAF’s ability to provide timely air support to ground troops operating in challenging environments. “The arrival of these five helicopters provides greater flexibility in the employment of airpower in support of ground troops in ongoing operations,” he said. The Air Chief expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his continued support for the transformation and modernisation of the NAF. Aneke said the Federal Government’s investment was enabling the service to progressively develop the capabilities required to meet its operational responsibilities and respond to Nigeria’s evolving security challenges. He said the three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters would significantly boost the NAF’s rotary-wing capabilities. He added that the platforms would enhance the service’s capacity for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), close air support, armed escort and combat search and rescue, as well as other joint missions in support of ground forces. “The versatility of the AW-109 platform is expected to provide commanders with additional options for rapidly deploying air assets in support of troops engaged in counter-terrorism, counter-insurgency and other internal security operations,” Aneke said. He said the helicopters would also improve the NAF’s ability to respond to emerging threats, particularly where speed, mobility and sustained aerial support were critical to ground operations. According to him, the two H-125 helicopters would complement the AW-109s by providing versatile light-helicopter capabilities for various operational requirements. The NAF said the platforms would collectively expand its flexibility and capacity to respond to changing operational demands, including moving personnel and equipment, conducting surveillance and supporting joint forces operating in difficult-to-reach areas. Helicopters Undergoing Assembly The NAF said the newly delivered platforms were undergoing post-delivery assembly and other technical processes ahead of their formal induction and operational deployment. The process, it added, would include crew-readiness and technical preparations required to ensure that the helicopters were fully prepared for operational employment. Aneke stressed that the NAF’s responsibility went beyond acquiring new platforms, noting that the service must ensure that the Federal Government’s investment translated into measurable operational results. He said the service would continue to prioritise effective employment, maintenance and logistics sustainment to ensure maximum availability of the aircraft. “We will continue to prioritise effective employment, maintenance and logistics sustainment so that every aircraft delivered adds measurable value to ongoing operations and the protection of the lives and property of Nigerians,” he said. The acquisition comes as the Armed Forces continue operations against terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security threats across multiple theatres. The NAF said the additional rotary-wing capacity would strengthen support for joint forces by improving the speed, reach and effectiveness of air support available to troops on the ground. The new helicopters are expected to enhance operational mobility, surveillance and responsiveness while supporting ground forces in their efforts to counter terrorists and other criminal elements. With the remaining seven AW-109 Trekker B helicopters expected before the end of 2026, the NAF is set to further expand its rotary-wing fleet and strengthen its capacity to provide air support for joint military operations. items.title: Ghana’s mineral resources must benefit host communities – Lands Minister
items.description: Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah Kofi-Buah, says Ghana’s mineral resources must generate tangible benefits for communities where mining activities take place. He said the overall outcome of mining activities across the country should be reflected in the development of host communities and contribute to the broader development goals of Ghana. The Minister made the remarks when a delegation from the North East Region paid a courtesy call on him at the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources on Tuesday, September 15, 2026. The engagement was aimed at exploring ways to streamline mining activities in the region and unlock its mineral potential. “Mineral resources must benefit the people there where the mining is taking place,” Mr Kofi-Buah said. Mining reforms The Minister said the government’s broader reforms in the mining sector are intended to improve the efficiency, effectiveness and governance of Ghana’s mineral resources. He said the administration of President John Dramani Mahama was introducing policies and programmes to ensure that the country’s mineral wealth is managed in a way that delivers greater value to Ghanaians. Mr Kofi-Buah also highlighted proposed changes to the prospecting and licensing regime, saying the practice of allowing a licence holder to prospect for as long as 30 years must give way to a system that creates opportunities for better-prepared investors. “That’s the new way forward,” he said. He welcomed the initiative by the overlord of the Mamprugu Kingdom, Naa Bohagu Mahami Abdulai Sheriga II , to engage government on developing the region’s mining potential. The delegation, led by the first elder of the Nayiri’s Palace, John Wuni Gruma , held discussions with the Ministry and the Minerals Commission on how to position the North East as a viable mining zone while ensuring that activities are properly regulated. Mr Kofi-Buah said he was hopeful the engagement would lead to a lasting partnership between the region and government. “I pray that this discussion will lead to a long term and lasting relationship,” he said. “You want us to work together to make sure we formalise things. It’s something that the Ministry and the Minerals Commission welcomes. We will look at what legally we can do,” he added. Minerals Commission to map potential The Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Commission, Isaac Tandoh , assured the delegation of the Commission’s commitment to identifying and developing the mining potential of the North East Region. He said the Commission would spearhead the mapping of mineralised zones using available geological data, alongside work on the appropriate licensing regime. Mr Tandoh said the Commission would apply existing regulations to establish a clear working relationship with the region and guide mining activities in line with the law. “The Commission had already visited the specific area identified to engage stakeholders,” he said, describing the delegation’s engagement with the Ministry as timely. Region commits to responsible mining The North East Regional Minister, Ibrahim Tia , who facilitated the engagement, said he had earlier visited mining sites across the region to caution illegal mining operators against activities that undermine government’s policies for developing the mining sector. He assured the Lands Minister that the delegation would report back to the Nayiri on the outcome of the discussions and the steps being taken to position mining as a driver of development in the region. “This is a dream that has come up severally and we were just looking for this opportunity,” Mr Tia said. “Consequently, we would work strictly according to the guidelines,” he added. Working committee established At the end of the meeting, Mr Kofi-Buah directed the formation of a working committee to facilitate the establishment of a new working relationship between the Ministry and the North East Region. The committee’s work will focus on addressing illegal mining activities while also developing an appropriate investment framework to attract responsible investors into the region. The broader objective is to ensure that the North East’s mineral resources are developed under a properly regulated framework and that mining contributes meaningfully to economic growth and development in host communities.

items.title: Le ministère des Habous refond les règles des marchés des "wakfs" publics
items.description: Le ministère des Habous et des Affaires islamiques a adopté un nouveau cadre réglementaire destiné à encadrer les marchés de travaux, de fournitures et de services conclus pour le compte des habous publics. Publié dans la dernière édition du Bulletin officiel, l’arrêté ministériel n° 348.26, daté du 24 chaabane 1447 (13 février 2026), redéfinit les règles de passation et d’exécution de ces contrats dans une logique de modernisation de la gestion des biens des « Wakfs « . Pris en application de l’article 147 du Code des habous et sur proposition du Conseil supérieur du contrôle financier des habous publics, ce texte vise à renforcer l’efficacité de la dépense, à rationaliser l’utilisation des ressources des « Wakfs » publics et à consolider les principes de gouvernance, de transparence et d’égalité d’accès à la commande. Le nouveau dispositif consacre plusieurs principes directeurs qui devront désormais présider à l’attribution des marchés. Parmi eux figurent la liberté d’accès à la commande, l’égalité de traitement entre les candidats, la garantie de leurs droits ainsi que la transparence dans les choix opérés par le maître d’ouvrage. Au-delà des exigences procédurales, le ministère entend également intégrer des objectifs plus larges dans la préparation et l’exécution des contrats. Les maîtres d’ouvrage sont ainsi tenus de prendre en considération les dimensions économiques, sociales, environnementales et écologiques des projets. Le texte insiste aussi sur la contribution aux objectifs de développement durable, à l’efficacité énergétique et à la préservation des ressources hydriques. La valorisation du paysage architectural, la protection du patrimoine national et des monuments historiques ainsi que la promotion de la recherche, du développement et de l’innovation figurent également parmi les orientations retenues. Certaines opérations demeurent toutefois exclues du champ d’application de cette réglementation. Il s’agit notamment des conventions relevant du droit commun, des partenariats entre les secteurs public et privé, des transferts de biens entre l’administration des habous et les établissements publics, ainsi que des actes relatifs aux biens des habous déjà encadrés par des arrêtés ministériels spécifiques conformément à l’article 60 du Code des habous. Le texte introduit par ailleurs un encadrement plus strict de la définition des besoins. Les maîtres d’ouvrage devront désormais les identifier en amont avec précision, en détaillant leur nature, leur volume et leurs caractéristiques techniques. Cette évaluation devra s’appuyer sur les normes marocaines en vigueur ou, à défaut, sur des standards internationaux reconnus. Dans le même esprit, les cahiers des charges ne pourront plus comporter de références à des marques commerciales, à des brevets ou à des sources déterminées susceptibles de limiter la concurrence. Une exception reste néanmoins possible lorsque cette référence est expressément justifiée et accompagnée de la mention « ou équivalent ». Le ministère impose également une série de vérifications préalables avant le lancement des procédures de mise en concurrence. Les maîtres d’ouvrage devront notamment s’assurer de la régularisation de la situation foncière des projets programmés et établir des estimations financières fondées sur les prix effectivement pratiqués sur le marché. Plusieurs modes contractuels sont désormais prévus. Le texte autorise notamment le recours aux marchés-cadres et aux marchés renouvelables pour les fournitures et services présentant un caractère récurrent, permanent ou prévisible. Ces contrats pourront être conclus pour une durée initiale d’un an et faire l’objet d’un renouvellement tacite, sans que la durée totale de reconduction n’excède trois années consécutives. Les seuils minimums et maximums devront toutefois être définis et encadrés. L’arrêté ouvre également la voie aux contrats associant conception et réalisation, une formule réservée en particulier aux projets techniquement complexes ou aux infrastructures spécifiques. Son utilisation reste soumise à une autorisation préalable de l’autorité compétente ainsi qu’au respect d’exigences visant à améliorer la performance énergétique des ouvrages. Afin d’élargir l’accès à la commande, le texte prévoit également la possibilité de diviser les marchés en lots distincts. Cette disposition vise à favoriser la participation des petites et moyennes entreprises, des coopératives et des auto-entrepreneurs. Le recours aux marchés à tranches conditionnelles est également introduit afin de permettre une exécution progressive des projets en fonction de la disponibilité des crédits programmés. L’une des principales innovations du nouveau dispositif réside dans l’introduction de la procédure dite de « dialogue compétitif ». Inspirée de mécanismes déjà utilisés dans plusieurs systèmes de commande publique, elle permet à l’administration des habous d’engager des discussions et négociations techniques, juridiques et financières avec les candidats présélectionnés. L’objectif est d’identifier les solutions les plus adaptées pour les projets complexes dont les contours ne peuvent être définis avec suffisamment de précision dès l’origine. Autre nouveauté notable : l’instauration du mécanisme des « offres spontanées ». Celui-ci permet aux entreprises, fournisseurs ou consultants de soumettre de leur propre initiative des projets ou des propositions innovantes répondant à des besoins qui n’ont pas encore été formalisés par l’administration. Lorsque ces propositions sont retenues puis intégrées dans une procédure concurrentielle ouverte, leurs auteurs bénéficieront d’un avantage sous la forme d’une majoration de 10 % de la note globale attribuée à leur offre. Le texte procède également à une clarification des modes de rémunération des marchés. Quatre catégories sont distinguées : les marchés à prix global, les marchés à prix unitaires, les marchés à prix mixtes et les marchés rémunérés sur la base de pourcentages. Cette dernière formule est toutefois limitée aux prestations architecturales. La question de l’évolution des prix fait également l’objet d’un encadrement détaillé. Les prix fermes demeurent la règle pour les marchés de fournitures et les prestations de services ne relevant pas des études. Des ajustements pourront néanmoins intervenir en cas de modification du taux de la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée ou de révision des prix de produits soumis à une réglementation spécifique. À l’inverse, les marchés de travaux ainsi que les contrats d’études dont la durée d’exécution dépasse trois mois devront obligatoirement prévoir des mécanismes de révision des prix, conformément aux règles applicables aux marchés publics de l’État. Enfin, l’arrêté limite strictement le recours aux prix provisoires. Ceux-ci ne pourront être utilisés que dans des situations exceptionnelles caractérisées par une urgence extrême, afin de garantir une meilleure maîtrise des engagements financiers liés aux marchés des « Wakfs » publics. À travers cette réforme, le ministère des Habous cherche à rapprocher la gestion des marchés des habous des standards contemporains de la commande publique, tout en introduisant de nouveaux outils destinés à encourager l’innovation, à renforcer la concurrence et à améliorer l’efficience des investissements réalisés à partir des ressources des habous publics. The post Le ministère des Habous refond les règles des marchés des "wakfs" publics appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘They are politically lazy’ – Wike tackles APC govs over Rainbow Coalition pushback
items.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has described governors of the All Progressives Congress as “politically lazy” following their opposition to his Rainbow Coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governors, led by their chairman and Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, had said they would not participate in, support or endorse any alliance that could undermine President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid or affect APC candidates at any level. But Wike, in an interview on Arise TV’s Prime Time on Tuesday, dismissed the concerns, arguing that his decision to support Tinubu did not mean he had abandoned his political party or agreed that other parties should not field candidates. “They are politically lazy. When you have your local problems, don’t use Mr President as your excuse,” Wike said. The minister maintained that the disagreements surrounding his political activities did not start with his decision to support Tinubu, recalling that he had faced opposition even when he was serving as governor of Rivers State and later as FCT minister. “This thing did not start today. It started at ministerial position. They were not happy that I was Minister of FCT. Also, they were unhappy when I was governor,” he said. Wike said his knowledge of the political situation was greater than that of those criticising his activities, suggesting that his critics would understand his position better if they had access to the information available to him. “If they know what I know, they would not come out to shout,” he said. The former Rivers State governor also insisted that his support for Tinubu remained unchanged, arguing that supporting the President was separate from the activities of his political party. “I have said I will support the President and I am still supporting him. What has that got to do with my party?” Wike asked. The minister further cited the political activities of governors such as Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo, Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke and Abia State Governor Alex Otti to argue that support for a presidential candidate should not prevent political parties from presenting candidates at other levels. “Take Soludo, Adeleke and Otti. Does it mean that their parties will not present other candidates? This thing they are saying does not have any basis,” he said. Wike also recalled the 2023 presidential election, saying his decision to support Tinubu was based on his belief that it was the South’s turn to produce the President after the Muhammadu Buhari administration. “Recall that in 2023, as far as the President is concerned, it is my belief that it was the time of the South and so it would be unfair that it goes back to the North,” he said. items.title: Wike’s Rainbow Coalition, APC govs backing Tinubu in different ways — Fayose
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Ekiti State Governor and Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, chieftain, Ayo Fayose, has said the controversy over the Rainbow Coalition being championed by Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, would not hurt President Bola Tinubu’s chances in the 2027 presidential election. Fayose said Wike and the APC governors were backing Tinubu in different ways, arguing that what mattered ultimately was whether the coalition could deliver votes for the president, particularly in Rivers State. He spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday amid renewed controversy over the Rainbow Coalition after APC governors warned against political arrangements capable of weakening the party’s candidates at various levels. The APC governors, led by Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum and Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, said on Monday that they would not support any alliance capable of undermining Tinubu’s re-election bid or APC candidates. Wike, however, reiterated on Tuesday that the Rainbow Coalition was a platform for politicians from different parties to support Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that it had nothing to do with the APC’s internal structure. Reacting to the controversy, Fayose said: “I sincerely don’t want to join issues on these two sides. “These are issues of simply everybody exercising their interest in the system. And everything I tell you again, is not about an NDC having an incursion as a result of what they are doing or ADC. No. “If Rainbow works for Wike in Rivers, and it can bring results, that’s all the president wants. “If Rainbow works and can give him numbers, you understand? So be it. The government says in our state, after all, Wike will not come to their states. Wike will not come there and vote. “He will not come there and form a coalition rainbow. And don’t let us deceive ourselves. Even in Nigeria. “It’s only that rainbow is in a particular state. Where the handler says, I can handle the rainbow. If the rainbow is to carry everybody along, guarantee everybody’s interest, ensure that, okay, if rainbow produces this, produces that, he will get this, you will get that. “As a man, who could flip an election, for a governorship candidate of people, and the PDP also could. If they have the capacity, and that they have done it, then he has capacity to do it in some states. The question is that, has he gone to any other state, to preach rainbow? No.” Fayose said the disagreement between Wike and the APC governors should not be interpreted as a threat to Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that political interests and individual egos were responsible for much of the controversy. “Everything works together for good, for the president. Without controversy, you can’t get far. Controversy in itself will help the election. “This controversy has nothing to do with the winning of the president. In fact, it makes it much better. Nigerians know who Wike is and the institution, the Nigerian Governors’ Forum and they are both saying different things in different ways. “Nigerian Governors’ Forum say we are not doing coalition, Wike says do what you have to do in your state. Whatever you feel comfortable with. If you are comfortable without a coalition, go ahead. “The method that works for A might not work for B. And this is not even playing to the hands of the opposition, because the two of them are united behind the president. And don’t forget, these are men of strength in our country. “You should expect this. The moment there is interest, power struggle, interest, you should expect all this. This has taken nothing out of the system. “That is the truth. This has taken nothing out of the system. So in my understanding, they all say the same thing in different ways. “But don’t forget, everybody has his own ego. Every one of us, including myself.” Fayose also addressed the difficulty of asking voters to support different political parties for different elective positions under a Rainbow Coalition arrangement, saying the strategy could work differently from one state to another. He maintained that Wike had not publicly presented himself as supporting candidates beyond the presidency while seeking to retain his influence within the PDP. “Wike has not put it out there that he is supporting people beyond the presidency because he still wants to keep the PDP. Wike has not hidden his position; neither have I hidden my position,” Fayose said. The former Ekiti governor further argued that the political calculations surrounding 2027 should be viewed within the context of Nigeria’s traditional practice of rotating political power. “The oppositions know they are going nowhere. The reality is that power is coming to the south for eight years. Tinubu is the shortest point of power going to the north,” he said. “Rotational presidency is not in our constitution but it is a norm nobody can shy away. If Obi becomes president, the north knows he will come back again after four years that the pressure from people wants him to continue,” Fayose added. His comments came as the Rainbow Coalition controversy intensified following the rejection of the arrangement by APC governors. The governors’ position has created a distinction between supporting Tinubu’s presidential bid and backing candidates outside the APC at governorship, National Assembly and state Assembly levels. Uzodimma said the governors’ campaign commitment remained exclusively to APC candidates. Wike, meanwhile, has maintained that the coalition is designed to mobilise support for Tinubu across party lines and does not amount to a parallel APC structure. items.title: Promiseland ends Tonto Dikeh’s ambassadorial deal
items.description: By Chioma Okoye Promise Land Innovation Limited, owners of the WEALTH App, has terminated its brand ambassadorship agreement with actress Tonto Charity Dikeh with immediate effect. The company announced the termination in a statement signed by its Executive Director, Mrs Gift Emmanuel, and dated September 15, 2026. According to the statement, the decision followed a review of Dikeh’s performance under the agreement, which the company said showed that contractual obligations and promotional objectives had not been satisfactorily fulfilled. The company also cited a performance review meeting scheduled for September 7, 2026, to review outstanding obligations and discuss the way forward. It said the meeting could not hold as scheduled because Dikeh did not attend. “Consequently, the Company has exercised its contractual right to bring the Brand Ambassadorship Agreement to an end with immediate effect,” the statement said. Promise Land Innovation Limited said Dikeh had been formally notified of the decision, adding that it wished her well in her future endeavours. The company said the termination would not affect its commitment to providing innovative solutions for real estate investment management through the WEALTH App. It thanked its subscribers, customers, partners and the general public for their continued interest, support and confidence in the platform. The company also reaffirmed its commitment to delivering innovative solutions designed to create lasting value for users. The post Promiseland ends Tonto Dikeh’s ambassadorial deal appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kudus makes first Tottenham start since January against Liverpool
items.description: Mohammed Kudus has been named in Tottenham Hotspur’s starting lineup for the first time since January as they face Liverpool in the Carabao Cup. The Ghana international has returned to action this season after recovering from injury, making three substitute appearances in the Premier League. Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi admitted ahead of the Liverpool clash that the 26-year-old is still short of full match fitness. Kudus’ start against Liverpool is therefore a major step in his recovery, with the extended minutes expected to help build his fitness and sharpness as he works his way back to his best.

items.title: Government launches five-year initiative to improve emergency maternal and newborn care
items.description: Government has launched a five-year Presidential Initiative on Maternal Health Emergency Response (PRIMER) as part of efforts to reduce maternal mortality and improve emergency care for pregnant women and newborns. Launching the initiative, Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang said Ghana has made progress in expanding access to maternal healthcare, with about nine in 10 women receiving at least four antenatal care visits and a similar proportion delivering in health facilities. She added that skilled health personnel attend about 86% of births. However, maternal mortality remains above the Sustainable Development Goal target of fewer than 70 deaths per 100,000 live births by 2030. Professor Opoku-Agyemang said this means Ghana’s next phase of the response must go beyond access to healthcare and focus on the quality, readiness and speed of care women receive. “Our focus must extend beyond service coverage to quality, readiness, speed,” she said. According to the Vice President, PRIMER is designed to address challenges that cannot be resolved by individual health facilities alone. These include financing, infrastructure, staffing, procurement, data and community mobilisation. “PRIMER is to help address obstacles that no single health institution can remove, whether in financing, infrastructure, staffing, procurement, data or community mobilization,” she said. The initiative will also identify interventions that are producing better maternal health outcomes and apply lessons from those interventions in other parts of the country. “PRIMER’s task is to identify what produces better outcomes in places like Dodua, strengthen the quality of care and apply those lessons where they can improve maternal survival,” Professor Opoku-Agyemang said. She cited Dodua as an example of what targeted interventions can achieve, recalling President John Dramani Mahama’s reference to a successful intervention during his first administration that brought maternal deaths in the area to zero. The Vice President questioned why maternal deaths continue to occur when many of the major causes are known and are largely preventable or treatable. “Where then is the gap?” she asked. PRIMER will focus on three broad areas: political leadership and social mobilisation; institutionalised accountability and evidence-based action; and sustainable domestic financing, alongside efforts to mobilise responsible external support. The initiative will strengthen maternal and perinatal death surveillance and response, improve the timeliness and quality of data, clarify institutional responsibilities and support regular high-level reviews of results. It will also cover maternity and newborn care, referral and transfer systems, access to blood, medicines and essential equipment, community engagement and the use of data to improve care. Professor Opoku-Agyemang stressed that maternal survival cannot be achieved by the health sector alone. She noted that factors such as roads, communication, transportation, water and energy can directly affect women’s ability to access timely and quality maternal healthcare. PRIMER will therefore work with institutions responsible for those areas to identify where existing programmes can contribute to improving maternal health outcomes and where gaps remain. The Vice President also called for stronger coordination among ministries, public institutions, local authorities, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, the private sector, development partners and communities. She said families and communities have an important role to play by encouraging women to seek care early, recognising danger signs and ensuring that women are supported rather than delayed when complications arise. Professor Opoku-Agyemang said the ultimate measure of PRIMER’s success should not simply be the number of women who access health facilities, but whether they survive childbirth and return home safely with their babies. “It is not enough for many more women to enter our health facilities. They must return home safely with their babies to their families.” Professor Opoku-Agyemang officially launched the Presidential Initiative on Maternal Health Emergency Response on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama.

items.title: President Mahama will hear about colts football now – GFA President at League launch
items.description: GFA President Kurt Okraku has reiterated his administration’s commitment to developing grassroots football in Ghana. Okraku made the remarks at the launch of the 2026/27 Colts Football League at the Ghanaman Soccer Centre of Excellence in Prampram on Tuesday. The GFA president referenced comments made by President John Mahama last week about the need to revive and strengthen Colts football, revealing that the Association was already working on a new vision for the development of the game at the grassroots level. Okraku said the GFA has invested significantly in Colts football over the past six years and believes its efforts have helped revive the competition. “Last week, our President spent time to speak about Colts football. I’m sure in his dreams, the Almighty God told him the GFA had planned to launch a Colts Football League today. Now, he will definitely hear about Colts football. “Ghana will be reminded that for six years running, we [GFA] have not only invested in Colts football, but we have also resurrected Colts football. We have introduced a lot of Colts-related activities than ever before.” The event was attended by key stakeholders in the Ghanaian football fraternity, including Ghana Football Association (GFA) Ambassador for Grassroots Football, Asamoah Gyan.

items.title: Koosin/Commune de Bourasso : La vente du poisson local, une activité lucrative
items.description: BURKINA-KOOSIN-PÊCHE-ARTISANALE Koosin/Commune de Bourasso : La vente du poisson local, une activité lucrative Bourasso, 14 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Installés aux abords du fleuve Vuhu, un affluent du Mouhoun, des pêcheurs et des commerçants proposent du poisson frais aux clients, une activité qui mobilise des hommes et des femmes de différents âges dans plusieurs villages riverains, a constaté l’AIB, ce lundi 14 septembre 2026. La vente de poisson frais est pratiquée depuis plusieurs années dans cette zone et constitue une importante source de revenus pour les pêcheurs, ainsi que pour les vendeurs et vendeuses installés le long du Vuhu. Parmi les espèces proposées figurent notamment le capitaine, la carpe, le silure et l’anguille. Chez les pêcheurs, le kilogramme de poisson est vendu entre 800 et 850 F CFA. Pour Ousmane Ouédraogo, un pêcheur venu de Dédougou, cette activité est particulièrement rentable. Il affirme la pratiquer depuis une quarantaine d’années. « J’ai deux sites, à savoir Bourasso et Sikoro. Depuis que j’ai commencé cette saison, je peux gagner entre 50 000 et 100 000 F CFA par jour », a-t-il déclaré. Du côté des commerçants, cette activité constitue également une source de revenus. Elisabeth Nana, une vendeuse venue de Dédougou et active depuis le début de la saison, dit tirer d’importants bénéfices de la vente du poisson. « Je ne me plains pas du tout. Ce commerce me permet de vivre dignement et de subvenir à mes besoins. Je peux réaliser entre 10 000 et 15 000 F CFA de bénéfice par jour. Les revenus de cette activité m’ont permis de réaliser quelques projets personnels », a-t-elle confié. Malgré sa rentabilité, la filière fait face à certaines difficultés, notamment la baisse du niveau d’eau du Vuhu. « Quand le niveau de l’eau baisse, le poisson devient rare. Il y a également l’impraticabilité de la voie Bourasso-Sikoro lorsqu’il pleut abondamment », a expliqué Ousmane Ouédraogo. Selon les acteurs, la réalisation de quelques aménagements simples pourrait contribuer à améliorer les conditions de cette activité et à renforcer la filière locale du poisson frais, tout en favorisant la création de revenus et le développement de l’économie locale. items.title: Minority says Foreign Ministry has failed to release GH¢50m evacuation records despite RTI request
items.description: The Minority in Parliament says the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has failed to provide detailed expenditure records on the nearly GH¢50 million spent on the evacuation and reintegration of Ghanaians from South Africa. The Minority Caucus on the Foreign Affairs Committee says it will therefore not participate in a closed-door meeting scheduled for Wednesday, September 16, unless the Ministry provides the itemised account and supporting documents it has requested. The meeting is expected to be addressed by Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa on the evacuation of Ghanaian nationals following xenophobic attacks in South Africa. In a statement signed by Damongo MP and Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, the Minority said it supported the government’s decision to evacuate Ghanaians whose safety and welfare had been threatened. “From the outset, the Minority supported government’s decision to evacuate Ghanaian citizens whose safety and welfare had been threatened by the unfortunate xenophobic attacks in South Africa.” However, the Caucus said its support for the evacuation does not relieve the government of its obligation to account for public funds used for the exercise. “That support, however, cannot dispense with the equally important obligation of Government to account fully and transparently for the expenditure of public funds.” The Minority said it submitted a formal request under the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989), on August 17, seeking comprehensive information on the cost and financing of the evacuation. The request was received by the Ministry on August 25. According to the statement, the request sought details on expenditure, funding sources, private partners and their contributions, flights and other transportation, accommodation, feeding, medical services and reintegration payments. It also requested relevant procurement and payment records. The Minority said the Minister announced on September 7 that almost GH¢50 million had been spent on the evacuation and reintegration of 1,964 Ghanaians. However, it says the Ministry has yet to provide the itemised account and supporting documentation needed to establish how the money was spent. “The expenditure of public funds carries with it a corresponding duty of accountability.” The Caucus said it does not consider it appropriate to attend a closed-door meeting on the evacuation while its formal request for the underlying expenditure records remains outstanding. It has consequently resolved not to participate in Wednesday’s meeting unless the requested documents are provided. The Minority has also reiterated its demand for full disclosure of the expenditure. “The Minority will remain resolute in the discharge of its constitutional and parliamentary responsibility to demand transparency and accountability in the use of taxpayers’ funds.”
